# Architectural rules, with what enforces each

<!-- generated by scripts/sync-agent-docs.mjs -- do not edit -->

> Generated from `workflow.ai.yml` by `node scripts/sync-agent-docs.mjs`. `AGENTS.md` carries the first
> sentence of each; this file carries all of it and what fails when it is broken.

- The core is framework-agnostic and platform-agnostic. Nothing under packages/core/src may import a node: module, a third-party package or another Indaba package; it imports only its own relative modules, so it runs in a browser as well as in Node. Node and every dependency live at the edges: the YAML parser, git and the span exporter (engine), processes and HTTP (runners), the command line (cli). A change that needs an exception belongs in infrastructure, behind an interface the domain owns.
  *Enforced by:* `packages/core/test/architecture.test.ts` (scans every import in the package), `packages/engine/test/layers.test.ts` and `packages/runners/test/layers.test.ts` (engine and runners may not reach upward), reviewed under dimension 1
- TypeScript runs strict with no escape hatch. tsconfig.base.json keeps strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes and verbatimModuleSyntax on; Biome keeps noExplicitAny, noTsIgnore and noNonNullAssertion at error. No any, no non-null assertion, and no suppression comment of any tool (@ts-ignore, @ts-expect-error, @ts-nocheck, biome-ignore, eslint-disable). A type the compiler cannot follow is fixed in the code, with a precise type, a narrowing function or a check at the boundary, never silenced.
  *Enforced by:* `scripts/security-audit.mjs` (suppression comments, any, non-null assertions, tsconfig and biome.json), `scripts/check-workflow.mjs` (the flags and rules stay as project states them), and CI (Verify on ubuntu-latest, windows-latest and macos-latest)
- The engine is deterministic. Given the same workflow, the same runner outputs and the same injected Clock and IdGenerator, a run takes the same steps in the same order and ends in the same state. Decision logic under packages/core/src and packages/engine/src reads no wall clock, no randomness and no environment: time arrives as a Clock, ids as an IdGenerator, configuration as constructor arguments. The edge files that own the system clock, the id source and git (git.ts, system.ts, jsonl-span-exporter.ts in the engine) are the only exceptions. DAG ordering breaks ties by declaration order, never by hash order.
  *Enforced by:* `scripts/security-audit.mjs` (determinism rules for those directories) and `packages/engine/test/layers.test.ts`; tie-breaking and replay by review (.agents/rules/review.md, dimension 2)
- Retry-loop isolation. When a step fails and on_failure retries a target, the next prompt receives only the isolated failure of the last attempt (the stderr or the failing assertion), never the accumulated error history. The retry count is bounded by max_retries, and a bounded exhaustion ends in the declared escalation, not another loop.
  *Enforced by:* review (.agents/rules/review.md, dimension 2); the engine's retry tests in packages/engine/test are the evidence a review asks for
- One runner contract. Every way of running an agent or a command implements the Runner interface from @indaba/core and returns a RunResult; the engine and the mesh depend on the interface and the registry, never on a concrete runner, and the command line composes the built-ins through the same PluginHost a third party uses. A runner owns its process or connection, honours the timeout and the AbortSignal, reports token usage when it knows it, and never leaks a child process (the whole process tree is killed on timeout or abort).
  *Enforced by:* `packages/engine/test/layers.test.ts` and `packages/runners/test/layers.test.ts` (the engine never imports the runners package); the contract itself by review (dimension 2)
- Secrets are never logged. API keys and tokens reach a runner through the environment of its own process or its own Authorization header and nowhere else: not in a trace attribute, an event, an exception message, a result artifact, a prompt or a log line. Every outgoing representation of a request redacts them.
  *Enforced by:* `scripts/security-audit.mjs` (credential shapes in source, committed .env files); redaction behaviour by review (dimension 4)
- No shell string interpolation of untrusted data. Processes are started with spawn or execFile and an argument array, with shell: false. The only code that may hand a string to a shell is the runner for commands the workflow author declared (ShellRunner), and nothing derived from a model's output, a file name, a branch name or an artifact path is concatenated into a command line. eval, new Function, the vm module, exec and execSync, and shell: true are banned everywhere.
  *Enforced by:* `scripts/security-audit.mjs` (banned constructs, and the shell interpreter allowlist that names only the ShellRunner file); the data flow into ShellRunner by review (dimension 4)
- Paths are confined. A path taken from a workflow file, a model, a guard or an artifact name is resolved against its root and rejected if it leaves it, before it is read, written, diffed or handed to git. Worktrees live under .indaba/worktrees/&lt;taskId&gt; and nowhere else, and teardown removes only what the manager created.
  *Enforced by:* review (.agents/rules/review.md, dimension 4); the confinement tests named in the owning spec
- Observability follows the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions. A task is a trace, a workflow step a span, an LLM call, a tool execution or a shell verification a child span, with gen_ai.* attribute names for the system, the model and the input and output token counts, and cost as a separate, documented attribute. The conventions are still developing; the attribute set in use is recorded in the observability spec, and a rename follows the convention, not taste.
  *Enforced by:* review (.agents/rules/review.md, dimension 5); the span and attribute tests of the observability feature
- Every feature has a specs/&lt;feature-name&gt;/ directory containing spec.md, api-surface.md and review.md. Each of plan.md, tasks.md, data-model.md, research.md and events.md is either written or named in spec.md under Artifacts not written, with the reason it does not apply.
  *Enforced by:* `scripts/check-workflow.mjs`; the track check holds a feature commit to it (`scripts/check-track.mjs`)
- Runtime dependencies are a recorded decision. The dependencies and optionalDependencies of the packages, apart from links between them, are exactly the packages project.runtime_dependencies and project.optional_dependencies name, and pnpm audit is clean. A new entry requires the decision in the feature's spec, because every one is a version Indaba can force onto a consumer's tree. @indaba/core has none.
  *Enforced by:* `scripts/check-workflow.mjs` (the lists against every package.json) and CI (Dependency audit)
- Public API changes are classified before they are written. Adding an export, an optional parameter or option with a default, or a method is a minor; changing a signature, a default, a member of a union, the workflow file schema, a CLI option or an emitted event or span attribute is a major. Record the classification in the spec and in CHANGELOG.md. Below 1.0 a major takes the next minor and says so.
  *Enforced by:* review (.agents/rules/review.md, dimension 3)
- Extension contracts live in @indaba/core, and built-ins get no privileged access. Runner, Guard, Plugin, PluginHost, EventDispatcher and their types are defined in core; engine, runners and the command line only compose them. The built-in runners and the git-diff guard register through the same PluginHost a third party's plugin gets, so adding a runner, a guard type or a listener never edits core, engine or runners.
  *Enforced by:* `packages/cli/test/plugins.test.ts` (a plugin registers a runner, a guard type and a listener from outside the packages) and `packages/core/test/extension.test.ts`, `packages/engine/test/layers.test.ts` and `packages/runners/test/layers.test.ts`; the no-privileged-access rule itself by review (dimension 1)
- One command, any OS. `pnpm qa` (Biome, tsc strict, Vitest) plus the node gates is the definition of done, and it runs natively on Windows, macOS and Linux with Node 22 and pnpm 9. A result from another Node major, another package manager or a stale node_modules is not evidence. Hooks, documentation and reports name the pnpm script, not a tool invoked by hand.
  *Enforced by:* `scripts/check-workflow.mjs` (the Node floor, the pnpm major and the scripts exist, and the CI os matrix equals project.supported_os); the pre-commit hook and CI both run pnpm qa, so a change that only works in one environment fails in CI
- Nothing is published or tagged unless the maintainer asks. A pushed v* tag runs the release workflow, which publishes the packages to npm with provenance and cannot be undone. An agent never pushes a tag, never runs npm publish, and says what a tag would start before the maintainer decides.
  *Enforced by:* review (.agents/skills/release/SKILL.md); the release workflow runs only on a pushed v* tag, and main is protected so the tag lands on a merged commit
- Repository documentation moves with the change: AGENTS.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md and specs/DEPENDENCY_MAP.md whenever the public surface, the architecture or the release contents change, and the files under docs/ in the same change as any added, removed or changed workflow field, guard, runner option, CLI option or default.
  *Enforced by:* review (.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md)
- Everything is tested, and coverage is at least 85% on statements, branches, functions and lines, measured by Vitest with the v8 provider over packages/*/src. New or changed behaviour ships with the tests that cover it, assertions of behaviour and not lines merely executed. The threshold is raised, never lowered, and an exclusion from coverage needs its reason written next to it in vitest.config.ts: a failing threshold is fixed with tests. Coverage is not the whole standard: end-to-end tests run the built CLI as a user does (pnpm e2e, in CI on every operating system), and mutation testing with StrykerJS (pnpm mutation, weekly and on demand) checks that the tests would notice a bug, a surviving mutant being fixed with a test.
  *Enforced by:* `pnpm qa` (the coverage thresholds in vitest.config.ts) and `scripts/check-workflow.mjs` (the thresholds stay at or above project.coverage_threshold and qa runs coverage); the end-to-end tests by the Verify jobs in CI; the mutation score by the Mutation tests workflow; whether the tests assert anything by review (dimension 7)
- No invented numbers. A token count, a cost or a duration that Indaba reports was measured or received from the provider, or is labelled an estimate with its source (the pricing table's date). A cost is never silently zero because a model is missing from the table: unknown is reported as unknown.
  *Enforced by:* review (.agents/rules/review.md, dimension 5)
